findings.citation: Logging on transitions only. The move to unavailable logs one ERROR naming the endpoint, the bucket and the cause (never the credentials); the move back logs one INFO.
findings.note: When a failed transfer makes storage unavailable, the only ERROR is the storage line naming operation and key, not endpoint or bucket. Add endpoint and bucket to that line (exactly one ERROR).

findings.citation: availability is checked once at startup and then only on demand, when an invoice page is opened and the last check is more than 30 seconds old, asynchronously, one check at a time; there is no background schedule (the human, 2026-10-17). The cost: right after the store changes state, the first page opened may still show the previous one;
findings.note: ADR still records ticket 1's one-shot startup check as the decision and defers to a ticket by name; not updated after the availability ticket.
An IOException reading the uploaded part answers 503 and calls markUnavailable(), pausing files for everyone until the next probe; spec scopes this to SdkException.
Spec gap: the Manager's detail page has no Attach control on main or this branch; story 21 and walkthrough steps 4 and 7 expect the Manager to attach there and see the attach wording.
findings.reason: human: the Manager does not attach; the spec was wrong and is corrected (stories 3, 21; steps 4, 7). Settled 2026-10-17.

findings.citation: docs/agents/coding-standards.md (Backend 12): "Table-driven tests (`@ParameterizedTest` + `@MethodSource`) for any method with more than two branch conditions, instead of copy-pasted per-case tests."
findings.note: configurationProblem has five branch conditions and is tested only through near-identical per-case Spring-context subclasses; blank access-key and secret-key branches untested. Fix: @ParameterizedTest + @MethodSource unit test over all five; keep one startup test proving the context survives.
data/ ignore removed; leftover local backend/data/ now untracked and could be committed by accident. Keep the ignore until those directories are gone.
Possible Duplicated Code: same 'HTTP status or exception simple name' expression in both; timeout override lambda repeated at ObjectStoreAvailability.java:141 and :150.
Possible Duplicated Code: same SeaweedFS image, credentials, docker run and wait loop in both scripts.
Possible Feature Envy: ObjectStoreConfig.configurationProblem reads only ObjectStoreProperties; move it onto the record.
Possible flag arguments: toResponse(invoice, false, false); boolean owned + (ExecutorService) cast; two constructors would remove them.
Possible layering smell: the service builds ResponseEntity with Content-Disposition and nosniff headers (HTTP translation outside the controller).
Possible Duplicated Code: three near-identical SDK-failure tests (put, read, delete); one parameterized test would do.

Paused Download is a role-less <span> with aria-disabled and (Manager) aria-label: not allowed/meaningless on a generic element in ARIA 1.2; screen readers likely read 'Download' with no disabled state or filename. Fix: plain muted text with a visually hidden filename, or role=link + aria-disabled=true without tabindex; DESIGN.md:202 wording to match.

Disabled Attach in the card header; the explaining notice is at the bottom of the card; a disabled button can't be focused. Spec accepts single notice; consider title/aria-describedby if Agents are confused.

findings.citation: Step 7: "Couldn't attach one or more files. Try again." and one ERROR in the backend log naming the store operation
findings.note: With the store down, attach returns 500 with an unhandled IllegalStateException ('Content input stream does not support mark/reset, and was already read once') from CarrierInvoiceFileStorage.put (SDK retry on a non-rewindable stream; not an SdkException so the catch misses it), a stack trace instead of one ERROR, and the store is not marked unavailable (next reload still enabled). Evidence: evidence/step-7-*.

findings.citation: Step 2: a PDF named `Réf "Oct" 2026 – Orange.pdf` ... listed and downloaded under exactly that name
findings.note: Through a browser upload the double quotes arrive as %22 (the browser percent-encodes " in the multipart filename), so the file is listed and saved as `Réf %22Oct%22 2026 – Orange.pdf`. Accents and en dash survive; bytes match.
findings.reason: human: browsers percent-encode quotes in multipart filenames before upload; accepted, the next feature uses computed names without quotes. Settled 2026-10-17.

findings.citation: spec.md:397 "void put(String key, MultipartFile file);   // streams the upload, size from the part"
findings.note: The F21 fix replaced RequestBody.fromInputStream with file.getBytes() + RequestBody.fromBytes, so each upload (up to 20MB) is held in memory. The spec allows whole-file in memory only for downloads. Stream and survive retries with RequestBody.fromContentProvider over file::getInputStream and file.getSize(), or have a human record the buffering.
